references.text: The use of 'sleep' as a metaphor for death, where God awakens the sleeping, parallels Jesus' statement that Lazarus has fallen asleep and He will wake him.
Describes those who sleep in the grave and cannot save themselves, emphasizing the need for an external agent (God/Jesus) to awaken them.
The prophecy about those who sleep in the earth and shall awake, either to eternal life or to shame, corresponds directly with Jesus' intention to raise Lazarus.
Jesus' own prophecy that those who are in the graves will hear His voice and come out is the theological background for the action in John 11.
Immediately before Lazarus is raised, Jesus defines Himself as 'the resurrection and the life,' giving meaning to the claim that He can awaken one who has fallen asleep.
Paul uses the same metaphor ('we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed') to describe the resurrection, linked to Jesus' victory over death.
